features.title: Fix PGRST102 heterogeneous-keys upsert (frozen large companies)
features.trigger: Live audit 2026-06-05: 1,139 companies (incl. SpaceX, OpenAI, Databricks, Carvana, DoorDash) failed their ENTIRE per-company jobs upsert every scan with `db_write: 400 PGRST102 "All object keys must match"`. 62,182 active jobs (59% of the index) were frozen — last_seen_at never refreshed, no new postings added — since 2026-05-17.
features.root_cause: PostgREST requires every object in a bulk insert/upsert array to carry an identical key set. The description hash-skip optimisation (landed 2026-05-17) attaches description/description_hash/description_fetched_at only to rows whose text changed, so any company with a MIX of changed + unchanged postings in one batch sent heterogeneous keys → 400 → whole-company write failed. Big boards (always ≥1 changed posting) failed every scan; the existing code fails safe by early-returning before the close-sweep, so jobs froze rather than being closed.
features.scope: src/scan.mjs probeOne(): bucket jobRows by their sorted key signature and upsert each homogeneous group separately. Any group failure still early-returns before the close-sweep (no close on partial write). Self-healing: the next successful scan re-stamps these companies and closes whatever the providers no longer list.
evidence: Proven on live prod mwcpoaefmggapztkxakp: 1,139 companies failing, 62,182 stale-open jobs, first_seen 2026-05-17 22:31. node --check passes.

VERIFIED LIVE 2026-06-05: ran the fixed scanner (scan f1a2b319) against prod — PGRST102 db_write failures 1,314 -> 0; 19-day freeze thawed (new=40,684 closed=10,214, stale-open 64,698 -> 10,024 with 0 stale among the 3,511 successful-write companies).
features.verify: select count(*) from public.probe_results pr join (select id from public.scans where status='ok' order by started_at desc limit 1) s on s.id=pr.scan_id where pr.error like 'db_write:%PGRST102%';  -- 0 on the fixed-code scan
features.next: MERGE PR #33 — the deployed cron still runs the old code, so the next scheduled scan re-freezes the mixed-description boards until merge (no data harm, just re-stales).

features.title: Server-side close-sweep (last_seen_at watermark RPC)
features.trigger: 1M-scale architecture review (claude-progress.md 2026-06-05): the close-sweep diffed a global in-Node snapshot of every active job and PATCHed a per-company external_id IN-list — O(total jobs) memory and a write wall at 10x, and the reason scans can't be sharded (double-close).
features.scope: Add public.close_unseen_jobs(company_id, scan_start) RPC: UPDATE jobs SET closed_at=now() WHERE company_id=$1 AND closed_at IS NULL AND last_seen_at < $scan_start. src/scan.mjs captures SCAN_START_ISO before any upsert and calls the RPC per successfully-probed company instead of the client-side diff. Idempotent, per-company → shard-safe (prerequisite for f-109 matrix sharding).
evidence: Migration applied to prod 2026-06-05; close_unseen_jobs('<fake-uuid>', now()) returns 0 (runs, non-destructive). Equivalence proven: across all 2,524 companies whose write succeeded last scan, 0 open jobs predate scan_start, so the watermark sweep closes exactly what the old diff did. node --check passes.
VERIFIED LIVE 2026-06-05 (scan f1a2b319): the RPC closed 10,214 jobs across companies with 0 over-closing — every one of the 3,511 successful-write companies ended with 0 stale-open jobs.
features.note: The in-Node snapshot is still read — it now serves only the description hash-skip and new-job counting, not closing. Dropping it entirely is coupled to the COPY/bulk-write work (f-110).
features.verify: select count(*) from pg_proc where proname='close_unseen_jobs';

features.title: Matrix-shard the scan (parallel jobs by company-hash)
features.trigger: The single ~30-min Actions job won't survive 10x company growth toward 1M jobs. Unblocked by f-108 (per-company server-side close-sweep), so parallel shards over disjoint companies never double-close.
features.scope: Stored companies.shard bucket [0,60) (generated, indexed). Shard i of N owns range [floor(i*60/N), floor((i+1)*60/N)) — tiles [0,60) exactly for any N<=60 (disjoint+complete). scan.mjs reads SHARD_INDEX/SHARD_COUNT and scopes the company load, the active-job snapshot (jobs!inner companies.shard), and the description pass to its slice; writes scans.shard_index/shard_count. Workflow uses a matrix; SHARD_COUNT derives from strategy.job-total so only the matrix list changes. Per-provider rate-limit concurrency is NOT divided by N (providers throttle per-IP; each shard runs on its own runner IP → ~N× aggregate throughput; adaptive limiter backs off if globally limited). f_new_jobs_by_scan_source windows on shard_index=0 so a sharded cycle isn't mis-bucketed.
evidence: Partition validated live (read-only): N=4 shards companies 898+921+887+957=3,663 (0 dupes) and jobs 25,860+25,107+25,138+29,634=105,739 (0 dupes) — disjoint AND complete. node --check passes. PostgREST and()/embedded companies.and() filter syntax verified against prod.

VERIFIED LIVE END-TO-END at N=2 (scans 5ffb7ec1 + 2fa87d8a): ran in parallel, 0 out-of-range probes either shard, union probed=3,663=total enabled, stale_among_healthy=0, active stable 105,737, new_jobs accurate (300), write_failed=0. Matrix reverted to default [0].

SCALED TO N=4 + VERIFIED LIVE (branch claude/f109-scale-shards-n4, dispatch 2026-06-11 23:19Z): matrix flipped [0]->[0,1,2,3], SHARD_COUNT=4 derived from strategy.job-total. All 4 shards status=ok; probed 895+918+885+954=3,652 = enabled set at scan-start; companies_write_failed=0 all shards. Partition disjoint+complete: owned-enabled per slice [0,15)/[15,30)/[30,45)/[45,60) = 895/918/884/954 = 3,651 total enabled, shard hashes span 0..59. Block-rate 0 (no 403/429/rate errors across 4x parallel runner IPs); only error all cycle = 1 HTTP 404 (slug drift, auto-disabled — unrelated to sharding). Active jobs 106,264 (no drop). Wall-clock ~3.5min (slowest shard 214s) vs ~6.5min unsharded.
features.status_note: Matrix now N=4 ([0,1,2,3]) on branch claude/f109-scale-shards-n4; validated live (4 shards green, 0 block-rate, partition disjoint+complete). Flips to 'shipped' on PR merge to main.

features.title: Job relevance layer (target-role classification + filtering)
features.trigger: Product is an AI-first staffing agency for tech/IT professionals, knowledge-workers, senior/exec leaders and students in those fields. The index was full of service/manual/retail/clinical noise (waiter, dishwasher, care assistant, automotive technician), mostly from SmartRecruiters' generic keyword seeding — roles our customers would never pay to be matched to.
features.scope: Classify every job by ROLE (not employer industry) into a family + is_target + seniority. Hybrid: src/classify.mjs high-precision rules (free, ~45% coverage) + gpt-4o-mini for the ambiguous middle (scripts/backfill-classification.mjs --llm). is_target NULL stays surfaced (only known-false hidden) so an unclassified backlog never hides good jobs. scan.mjs classifies new jobs at ingest and gates description/embedding spend to is_target is not false. match_resume(_candidates) filter is_target is not false.
evidence: Rules validated on 105k live titles: 45.5% high-precision (33.9% target, 11.6% non-target). Ran rules backfill: 48,162 tagged. 12,259 known-noise jobs now hidden from matching (not.is.false=93,603 surfaced). node --check passes; not.is.false filter verified live.

The 55% null bucket is where blue-collar still leaks (sampled misses: 'Food and Beverage Attendant', 'Auto Body Repair Technician', 'Licensed Practical Nurse', 'Mental Health Therapist', 'Distribution Technician'). Blue-collar caught by family: clinical 5,170 / trades 1,753 / manual 1,750 / service 1,629 / retail 1,558. See docs/blue-collar-filtering.md.

features.title: Parameterize relevance in search (target_only/family filters) — two-product backbone
features.trigger: Two products share one DB + one search engine (HOSTED_PLATFORM_PLAN.md 'one DB, two lenses'). Staffing wants tech-only; the agent/NL MCP wants the whole index. Relevance must be a query parameter, not baked in.
features.scope: Replace the hardcoded `is_target is not false` in match_resume/match_resume_candidates with parameters (target_only boolean default true, optional family/seniority/location/remote/comp filters). Add a generalised search_jobs(query_vec, filters) RPC both products call. Staffing passes target_only=true (default, so today's path is unchanged); Product B passes target_only=false + any filters.
features.hard_filter_note: These hard constraints (seniority band, comp floor, location, work-auth) must be SQL predicates, NOT embedded text — today they're embedded in buildJobText so seniority/comp get soft-matched (the 'senior roles to a new grad' risk). With tight filters on the 1M HNSW, use pgvector 0.8 iterative index scan or partial indexes to avoid the pre/post-filter recall cliff (we already lift hnsw.ef_search). See docs/matching-embedding-assessment.md.
features.next: Land alongside the launch so staffing keeps target_only=true while the engine is ready for Product B.

features.title: Embeddings across the index (matchability)
features.trigger: The matcher only sees embedded jobs. Live check 2026-06-05: of 93,847 surfaced target jobs only 7,249 (7.7%) are embedded — clients are matched against 8% of the index. Biggest single lever on product quality and the #1 launch blocker.
features.scope: Run summary + embedding backfill. LAUNCH ORDER: classify (LLM) -> embed the tech/target slice first (~36k, cheap) to launch staffing (Product A); then embed the full index for Product B's NL search. Also decide ongoing freshness: enable LLM passes in cron OR a daily classify->summarize->embed backfill, else new jobs are unmatchable within days.
features.note_2026_06_12: Embedding coverage alone is necessary but NOT the biggest accuracy lever — the bake-off shows the two-stage reranker (f-122) is +10.9 meanFit / +30 recall over dense cosine, which is dead-last of 10 methods. Embed the TARGET slice first (don't embed blue-collar that's filtered out) then ship f-122. See docs/matching-embedding-assessment.md.

The multi-KB description is the TOAST-heavy part of a jobs row (jobs total ~891MB: 112MB heap + 179MB index + ~600MB TOAST), driving update-amplification and the backup/PITR bill (docs/scaling-architecture.md). Do the structural moves while the table is still small (157k rows) and cheap to rewrite.
features.scope: Step 1 (DONE): mirror jobs.description into a narrow public.job_descriptions(job_id pk, company_id, description, updated_at), kept in lockstep by an AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF description trigger (sync_job_description). 148,417 rows backfilled (every job with a non-empty description; still_missing=0). Step 2 (DONE): convert public.jobs to 16-way HASH partitioning on company_id — the only key compatible with the scanner's ON CONFLICT (company_id, external_id) upsert, keeps dedup exact and never moves a row between partitions. features.title: Hybrid retrieval arm: lexical GIN index + search_jobs_hybrid RPC (RRF)
features.scope: Additive lexical/BM25 arm to feed a second-stage reranker in the ops-console (bake-off rec #2). New GIN expression index over to_tsvector(title + description_summary); new RPC search_jobs_hybrid(query_vec, lexical_query, filters) that runs a dense (HNSW cosine) arm + a lexical (websearch_to_tsquery/ts_rank_cd) arm over a shared filtered base and fuses them with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60). Returns richer rows (title, description_summary, seniority, comp_*) so the Worker can rerank on text + score soft comp/seniority signals without N get_job round-trips. Hard filters kept minimal (closed_at, embedding, targetOnly, opt-in remote, since); NO compFloor/families/seniority predicates (sparse / vocab-mismatched -> soft signals in fyj). search_jobs / get_job / match_resume* untouched (Product B + CLI contract).

features.notes: Lexical strength tracks the description_summary backfill (degrades to title-only on unsummarised rows). Embedding model unchanged (text-embedding-3-small) — Voyage is rerank-only on the fyj side, so no re-embed.
